thread:
alex: Quick sync — we have a key customer asking for deterministic, comparable scores from the rerank endpoint so they can run experiments across datasets. Need decisions on: top_k semantics, what normalization we expose, truncation order, and launch acceptance criteria. Who's on?
maria: I can drive the ML side. Two immediate choices for normalization: softmax (probabilities) vs min-max per-list. Both have pros/cons. Customer wants stable deltas when list size varies.
samir: Softmax gives probabilistic interpretation but is sensitive to list size and temperature. Min-max gives a fixed [0,1] range but is affected by outliers. Another option: return raw_score + normalized_score so downstream can pick.
jordan: Returning two scores is fine but increases response payload. Could make normalized_score optional via param `include_normalized=true|false`. Also need to decide `top_k` semantics: should server filter to top_k before sending, or should we always return all scores and let clients slice? For most customers, server-side `top_k` reduces bandwidth and cost.
kyle: Truncation concern: when candidates are long (docs/snippets) we need deterministic truncation so results don't jitter. Proposal: keep full query, then truncate candidate contexts to max_total_tokens per-request. Default policy: right-trunc of candidate text (keep start). We could add `truncation_strategy` choices: `right_trunc`, `left_trunc`, `semantic_closest` (slow).
alex: Triage tradeoffs: payload vs reproducibility vs cost. For launch we should aim for a conservative API that supports experimentation without breaking existing integrations. Draft acceptance criteria: 1) doc + SDK updates complete, 2) p95 latency for common list sizes <= baseline + 20ms, 3) precision@k not worse than current by >2% on our eval set, 4) cost regression <= 5%.
maria: Implementation detail: normalized_score = softmax(raw_scores / temperature) computed with stable log-sum-exp. Expose `temperature` with default 1.0 and clamp in [0.1, 5]. Also add `normalization_method` param with values `softmax` or `minmax` (default `softmax`).
samir: Example payload suggestion for clarity:```json
{ "query": "...", "candidates": [ {"id":"c1","text":"..."}, {"id":"c2","text":"..."} ], "top_k": 10, "include_normalized": true, "normalization_method": "softmax" }
```Example response:```json
{ "items": [ {"id":"c2","raw_score": -1.23, "normalized_score": 0.76}, {"id":"c1","raw_score": -2.44, "normalized_score": 0.24} ], "meta": {"model":"redwood-rerank-v1","top_k":10} }
```
jordan: For backward compatibility: if `include_normalized` omitted, default to `false` to avoid changing payload shape for current customers. But product and docs should recommend opt-in. Also add `return_all=true` for evaluation customers who want every candidate + score.
kyle: Deterministic tie-breaker: preserve original candidate order when scores equal (stable sort). Also for truncation, record `truncation_metadata` in response when we cut candidate text so customers can audit why something lost context. Maybe `truncated: true` and `original_length` fields.
alex: Rollout plan: prototype PR (eng-ml) in 2 weeks, API + SDK changes (eng-platform) in 3 weeks, internal dogfood + eval for 2 weeks, canary at 10% traffic with feature flag for 4 weeks, GA at week 8 if metrics look good. Owners: maria (eng-ml lead), jordan (eng-platform), alex (product).
maria: Metrics to monitor during canary: ordering flip rate vs baseline, precision@k, p95 latency, avg tokens per request, errors. Suggest adding an automated regression alert if ordering flip > 5% on held set.
samir: Dev note: store raw_scores and normalization params (method + temperature) in logs so we can reproduce client-reported diffs. We should also log seed for any nondet ops.
jordan: SDK change: add `RerankOptions` with fields `top_k`, `include_normalized`, `normalization_method`, `temperature`, `return_all`, `truncation_strategy`. Keep defaults backward compatible.
kyle: Edgecases: identical text, extremely long candidate lists (>200). For big lists, we may refuse `return_all` or enforce pagination and a max candidates limit. Propose server max_candidates=500.
alex: Decision summary (for the record): default server-side `top_k` = 10; support `top_k` param; default `include_normalized=false` but enable `normalized_score` via opt-in param; default `normalization_method=softmax` with `temperature` param; expose `truncation_strategy` and include `truncation_metadata` when truncation occurs; stable tie-breaker = original order. Owners + timeline as above.
maria: I'll open the implementation PR with unit tests and a small eval harness.
samir: I'll add logging/tracing hooks for per-request normalization details.
jordan: I'll scope SDK + docs work. Will also add canary feature flag.
kyle: I'll draft the truncation strategies and edgecase handling doc.
alex: Thanks — will send this as the decision note and add to roadmap. :thumbsup:
